Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: update the decompose-run ID in the smoke canary

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8641` @ `cec39fdb5f94ab267130b2f79c6604870cfce49c` (Integration branch mismatch: false)

## Files likely to change
- `tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt`

## Functions or modules to implement
- None. This is a data-only edit. Change line 2 of the canary from `decompose-run: 40427433026` to `decompose-run: 41367073667`. Line 1 stays `status: ok`, and the file keeps its trailing newline.

## Data structures affected
- The plain-text canary file. It is two LF-terminated lines (I checked with `cat -A`).

## API or interface changes
- None.

## Decisions
### D1 — Do not edit the advisory "Expected files" test modules
- Chosen: edit only `tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt`.
- Alternatives considered: also update the 11 Python tests listed in the decomposition.
- Why: the issue's scope section forbids touching any other file. None of those tests contains the string `40427433026`, so none of them pins the old ID. They only refer to the canary file by name, so changing its contents cannot break them.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundaries, endpoints or external inputs are involved. Abuse case: a wider diff in this PR would break scope-lock. The edit is limited to one file to prevent that.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- Conflict noted: the "Expected files" list names 11 test modules, but the issue's scope says to modify only the canary. The scope section is followed.
- The trailing newline must be kept so that `wc -l` reports 2.

## Testing considerations
- Check that `head -n1` prints `status: ok`.
- Check that `sed -n 2p` prints `decompose-run: 41367073667`.
- Check that `wc -l` reports 2.
- Check that `git diff --stat` lists only `tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt`.
- Optionally run `pytest` on the test modules that reference the canary.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt
Scope-mode justification: the issue spells out exactly what to change, and it is a one-line edit to an existing file. There are no new helpers or patterns, and a complete fix costs the same as a shortcut, so nothing in the "Boil the Lake" rule calls for expanding scope. Under the §6 priorities (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the smallest exact edit is also the correct one.
